responsibility: Own the SQLite schema, migrations and every read/write path for runs, per-stage run status, raw payloads, enriched features, tags and analysis results. No other module issues SQL.
changelog: 0.2.0 - Added the run_stages table and its three accessors to support stage-granular resume (ADR-014). Added the EventSink protocol, which acquisition, enrichment and analysis already type-hint against but which had no owning module. Added the write-ordering invariant required by ADR-016.

tables.schema_meta: version INTEGER NOT NULL, applied_at TEXT NOT NULL
tables.runs: run_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, started_at TEXT NOT NULL, finished_at TEXT, status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(status IN ('pending','running','succeeded','failed','cancelled')), trigger_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'manual' CHECK(trigger_type IN ('manual','scheduled')), parent_run_id TEXT REFERENCES runs(run_id), config_json TEXT NOT NULL, parameters_version TEXT NOT NULL, code_version TEXT, error_message TEXT, notes TEXT
tables.run_stages: run_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(run_id) ON DELETE CASCADE, stage TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(stage IN ('acquisition','enrichment','analysis')), status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(status IN ('pending','running','succeeded','failed','cancelled')), started_at TEXT, finished_at TEXT, attempt INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, error_message TEXT, PRIMARY KEY (run_id, stage)
tables.run_events: event_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, run_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(run_id) ON DELETE CASCADE, ts TEXT NOT NULL, stage TEXT NOT NULL, level TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(level IN ('debug','info','warning','error')), message TEXT NOT NULL, progress REAL
tables.raw_games: run_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(run_id) ON DELETE CASCADE, appid INTEGER NOT NULL, source TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(source IN ('steamspy_all','steamspy_appdetails','steam_appdetails','steam_reviews')), fetched_at TEXT NOT NULL, http_status INTEGER NOT NULL, payload_json TEXT NOT NULL, payload_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (run_id, appid, source)
tables.games_enriched: run_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(run_id) ON DELETE CASCADE, appid INTEGER NOT NULL, name TEXT, app_type TEXT, developer TEXT, publisher TEXT, release_date TEXT, price_usd REAL, is_free INTEGER, review_count INTEGER, review_positive_pct REAL, owners_estimate_low INTEGER, owners_estimate_mid INTEGER, owners_estimate_high INTEGER, size_bytes INTEGER, achievement_count INTEGER, language_count INTEGER, platform_count INTEGER, dlc_count INTEGER, dev_title_count INTEGER, is_early_access INTEGER, early_access_days INTEGER, deck_compat TEXT, genres_json TEXT, categories_json TEXT, complexity_score REAL, imputed_features_json TEXT, estimated_sales_low REAL, estimated_sales_mid REAL, estimated_sales_high REAL, estimated_revenue_gross_usd REAL, estimated_revenue_net_usd REAL, effort_adjusted_return REAL, parameters_version TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (run_id, appid)
tables.game_tags: run_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(run_id) ON DELETE CASCADE, appid INTEGER NOT NULL, tag TEXT NOT NULL, votes INTEGER, rank INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY (run_id, appid, tag)
tables.analysis_results: run_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(run_id) ON DELETE CASCADE, analysis_type TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, parameters_version TEXT NOT NULL, payload_json TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (run_id, analysis_type)

schema.index_notes: run_stages needs no secondary index: its primary key (run_id, stage) already serves the only access pattern, which is 'all stages of one run'.

public_interface.name: get_connection
public_interface.signature: def get_connection(db_path: Path) -> sqlite3.Connection
public_interface.description: Opens a connection with the required pragmas, in autocommit mode (isolation_level=None) so explicit transactions are started explicitly. One connection per thread; never share across threads.

public_interface.name: connect
public_interface.signature:
@contextmanager
def connect(db_path: Path) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]
public_interface.description: Context-manager form of get_connection that guarantees close() on exit. This is the form the UI uses once per Streamlit rerun and the form the pipeline worker thread uses for its own connection (ADR-016).

public_interface.name: initialize_schema
public_interface.signature: def initialize_schema(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None
public_interface.description: Creates all tables and indexes if absent and stamps schema_meta. Idempotent. Does not pre-create run_stages rows; those are created lazily on first attempt of a stage.

public_interface.name: current_schema_version
public_interface.signature: def current_schema_version(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> int

public_interface.name: migrate
public_interface.signature: def migrate(conn: sqlite3.Connection, target_version: int | None = None) -> int
public_interface.description: Applies ordered migrations inside a transaction. Returns the resulting version.

public_interface.name: create_run
public_interface.signature: def create_run(conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, config: dict, parameters_version: str, trigger_type: str = 'manual', parent_run_id: str | None = None, code_version: str | None = None, notes: str | None = None) -> str
public_interface.description: Inserts a run row with status 'pending' and returns the generated run_id (UTC timestamp prefix plus short random suffix, sortable and human-readable).

public_interface.name: update_run_status
public_interface.signature: def update_run_status(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, status: str, *, finished_at: str | None = None, error_message: str | None = None) -> None
public_interface.description: Committed immediately. Per the ADR-016 write-ordering rule this must be the last write of the unit of work it describes.

public_interface.name: begin_run_stage
public_interface.signature: def begin_run_stage(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, stage: str) -> int
public_interface.description: Upserts the (run_id, stage) row to status 'running': sets started_at, clears finished_at and error_message, increments attempt, and returns the new attempt number. Committed immediately so the UI sees the stage transition. Re-attempting a stage that already succeeded is legal and is how resume and a post-parameter-change stage re-run work (ADR-009, ADR-014).

public_interface.name: finish_run_stage
public_interface.signature: def finish_run_stage(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, stage: str, status: str, *, error_message: str | None = None) -> None
public_interface.description: Writes the terminal status for one stage ('succeeded', 'failed' or 'cancelled') plus finished_at. Must be called only after that stage's own data writes have been committed (ADR-016).

public_interface.name: read_run_stages
public_interface.signature: def read_run_stages(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str) -> list[RunStage]
public_interface.description: Returns one row per stage that has been attempted, ordered by pipeline order (acquisition, enrichment, analysis). A stage never attempted is absent from the list rather than synthesised as 'pending', so callers can distinguish 'not started' from 'started and pending'.

public_interface.name: get_run
public_interface.signature: def get_run(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str) -> RunRecord | None

public_interface.name: list_runs
public_interface.signature: def list_runs(conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, limit: int = 50, offset: int = 0) -> pd.DataFrame
public_interface.description: Run list for the Past Analyses page, newest first, with candidate counts joined in.

public_interface.name: delete_run
public_interface.signature: def delete_run(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str) -> None
public_interface.description: Explicit user action only. Cascades to all run-keyed tables including run_stages.

public_interface.name: append_run_event
public_interface.signature: def append_run_event(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, *, stage: str, level: str, message: str, progress: float | None = None) -> int
public_interface.description: Append-only progress record. Committed immediately so a reader thread can observe it. Per ADR-016 it is written after the data it announces, never before.

public_interface.name: read_run_events
public_interface.signature: def read_run_events(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, *, since_event_id: int = 0) -> list[RunEvent]
public_interface.description: Incremental read for UI polling. The caller keeps the highest event_id it has seen and passes it back.

public_interface.name: EventSink
public_interface.signature:
class EventSink(Protocol):
    def __call__(self, *, stage: str, level: str, message: str, progress: float | None = None) -> None: ...
public_interface.description: Structural type for the progress callback that orchestration passes into every stage entry point. acquisition.run_acquisition, enrichment.run_enrichment and analysis.run_analysis already type-hint their on_event parameter against this name. It is declared here rather than in orchestration because the stage modules must not import orchestration; that would invert the dependency direction. The concrete implementation is built by orchestration and normally wraps append_run_event.

public_interface.name: upsert_raw_payloads
public_interface.signature: def upsert_raw_payloads(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, payloads: Iterable[RawPayload]) -> int
public_interface.description: Batched insert inside one transaction, INSERT OR IGNORE on the (run_id, appid, source) key. Returns rows written. The IGNORE semantics are what make re-running acquisition for the same run_id an insert-missing operation rather than an in-place update, so ADR-005 immutability holds while resume stays cheap.

public_interface.name: read_raw_payloads
public_interface.signature: def read_raw_payloads(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, source: str) -> Iterator[RawPayload]
public_interface.description: Streams rows; must not materialize the whole catalog snapshot in memory.

public_interface.name: read_fetched_appids
public_interface.signature: def read_fetched_appids(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, source: str) -> set[int]
public_interface.description: Appids already persisted for this run and source. acquisition uses it to skip work when a stage is re-attempted after a crash or cancellation (ADR-014).

public_interface.name: write_enriched
public_interface.signature: def write_enriched(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, frame: pd.DataFrame) -> int
public_interface.description: Replaces the run's enriched rows transactionally.

public_interface.name: read_enriched
public_interface.signature: def read_enriched(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, *, columns: Sequence[str] | None = None, where: str | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame

public_interface.name: write_tags
public_interface.signature: def write_tags(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, rows: Iterable[TagRow]) -> int

public_interface.name: read_tags
public_interface.signature: def read_tags(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, *, min_votes: int = 0) -> pd.DataFrame

public_interface.name: write_analysis_result
public_interface.signature: def write_analysis_result(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, analysis_type: str, payload: dict, *, parameters_version: str) -> None
public_interface.description: Upsert on (run_id, analysis_type), so re-running the analysis stage for an existing run replaces its prior outputs.

public_interface.name: read_analysis_result
public_interface.signature: def read_analysis_result(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, analysis_type: str) -> dict | None

invariants: raw_games rows are never updated in place; re-attempting a stage inserts only the rows that are missing, and a correction still requires a new run
All timestamps are stored as ISO-8601 UTC strings
Every write that spans more than one row runs inside a single transaction
run_id is sortable lexicographically by start time
Write ordering (ADR-016): the data of a unit of work is committed before the run_events record or run_stages / runs status that announces it. Status and event writes are always last, never first
run_stages rows are created lazily; a stage that was never attempted has no row at all
Connections are opened in autocommit mode so a polling reader never pins a stale WAL snapshot inside a long-lived implicit read transaction
edge_cases: Database file or parent directory missing -> created on first get_connection
Concurrent read while the pipeline writes -> supported via WAL; reader must tolerate a partially populated run
Connection reused across threads -> must raise, not silently corrupt (check thread identity)
Very large payload_json rows -> insert in batches; avoid loading all payloads at once
delete_run on an unknown run_id -> no-op, not an error
delete_run cascades to run_stages along with the other run-keyed tables
Empty enriched frame passed to write_enriched -> writes zero rows and returns 0 without raising
begin_run_stage on a stage whose row is already 'succeeded' -> attempt incremented, status reset to 'running', finished_at and error_message cleared; this is legal
finish_run_stage for a stage that was never begun -> StorageError, because it would record a terminal status with no start time
read_run_stages on a run where no stage was ever attempted -> empty list, not an error
upsert_raw_payloads re-inserting an appid/source already present for the run -> ignored, counted as zero rows written, never overwritten

unit: initialize_schema is idempotent and produces the expected table and index set, including run_stages
migrate from an older fixture database reaches the current version and preserves rows
create_run returns lexicographically sortable ids and round-trips through get_run
append_run_event / read_run_events with since_event_id returns only newer events
begin_run_stage increments attempt across repeated calls and read_run_stages returns stages in pipeline order
finish_run_stage records the terminal status and finished_at, and stores error_message only for failed or cancelled
finish_run_stage on a never-begun stage raises StorageError
upsert_raw_payloads stores payloads verbatim (byte-equal JSON round-trip) with correct sha256
upsert_raw_payloads is insert-missing: a second call with an overlapping batch writes only the new rows and leaves the existing payload bytes unchanged
read_fetched_appids returns exactly the appids persisted for that run and source
write_enriched then read_enriched preserves dtypes and NULL handling for missing features
delete_run cascades to run_stages, raw_games, games_enriched, game_tags, analysis_results and run_events
integration: a full write/read cycle of one small synthetic run across all tables, including a stage that is begun, failed, re-begun and then succeeded

non_goals: No business logic, no derived value computation
No automatic pruning or retention policy
No knowledge of pipeline ordering beyond the stage name CHECK constraint; deciding which stage runs next is orchestration's job
open_questions: Should payload_json be zlib-compressed once the database exceeds a size threshold, or from the start?
